question: Does a birth chart show Steiner's "world-view constellations"?
what_the_sources_say: Steiner (GA 151, lecture 4) says these soul constellations matter more than the outer horoscope and need not coincide with the nativity.
rule_the_app_follows: The app shows each planet's mood and its constellation's world-view as a prompt for reflection only. It never claims that the birth chart determines a person's outlook.

question: Senses to zodiac: two different lists
what_the_sources_say: The 1913 lesson (GA 265a) puts speech in Aries, self in Gemini, touch in Cancer, life in Leo, balance in Libra, warmth in Aquarius and hearing in Pisces. The 1921 sketch (as reproduced by Soesman) puts ego in Aries, word in Gemini, hearing in Cancer, warmth in Leo, balance in Sagittarius, life in Aquarius and touch in Pisces. Steiner never gives a full list in a lecture.
rule_the_app_follows: The 1921 sketch is the default; the 1913 list can be selected in Settings. In the 1913 notes, Capricorn = sight only by elimination.

question: Steiner's exchange of the names Mercury and Venus
what_the_sources_say: Steiner said several times that medieval occultists deliberately swapped the names, so "occult Mercury" = astronomical Venus and vice versa (secondary: AnthroWiki "Occult order of planets").
rule_the_app_follows: Planet moods (GA 151) and eurythmy vowels are applied to the bodies under their astronomical names, exactly as Steiner printed them. For the life spheres (Mercury 7–14, Venus 14–21) the app names both bodies.

question: Ophiuchus
what_the_sources_say: Steiner, Vreede and Sucher all worked with twelve constellations; none of them gives a world-view for Ophiuchus. The IAU boundaries put about 18° of the ecliptic in Ophiuchus.
rule_the_app_follows: A body in the Ophiuchus band is read as a transition between Dynamism (Scorpio) and Monadism (Sagittarius), and is clearly labelled as an app rule.

question: Bodies far from the ecliptic (e.g. the Moon or Venus in Orion, Cetus, Sextans)
what_the_sources_say: The IAU constellation at a body's true position may be non-zodiacal. Sucher placed bodies by their ecliptic longitude against the fixed-star zodiac.
rule_the_app_follows: The reading uses the zodiac band, i.e. the IAU constellation on the ecliptic at the body's longitude. The true IAU constellation is also shown and flagged.

question: IAU (unequal) constellations vs. equal 30° sidereal signs
what_the_sources_say: Sucher drew the "real constellations ... more or less in its actual extent" (1937), alongside the tropical signs. Powell later used equal 30° sidereal signs. The IAU 1930 boundaries are a modern convention that none of them used.
rule_the_app_follows: The IAU 1930 boundaries are used throughout, with 13 bands including Ophiuchus. The app also shows tropical longitude for comparison.

question: Hermetic Rule: which direction of the Moon's course; premature births
what_the_sources_say: Sucher 1937: waxing Moon → epoch Moon at the birth Ascendant; waning → at the Descendant. About 273 d (10 sidereal months); for a seven-month child use 8 months (≈218 d).
rule_the_app_follows: The app searches the window 10 (or 8) sidereal months ± half a month before birth for the moment the Moon reaches the target longitude. Within that window the solution is unique, and it reproduces Sucher's four cases.

question: Does the epoch Ascendant have to equal the birth Moon?
what_the_sources_say: The full classical rule (trutina Hermetis) is reciprocal: the birth Moon gives the Asc/Desc at the epoch. Sucher (Spiritual Nativity) cites this. In practice it is used to correct the recorded birth time.
rule_the_app_follows: The app reports the residual (degrees) between the epoch Asc/Desc and the birth Moon, and does not correct the birth time automatically.

question: Prenatal Moon cycles → seven-year periods
what_the_sources_say: Sucher 1937 (Wagner): the first lunar cycle after the epoch reflects ages 0–7, the next 7–14, and so on. The cycles are counted by the Moon's returns to its epoch position among the fixed stars.
rule_the_app_follows: Each sidereal return of the Moon to its epoch longitude opens the next seven-year period. Within a cycle, age is mapped linearly (fraction of the cycle × 7 years).

question: Geocentric vs heliocentric
what_the_sources_say: Sucher (Practical Approach) treated heliocentric and geocentric views as complementary.
rule_the_app_follows: Both views are shown. Moods and world-views apply to the geocentric reading; the heliocentric wheel is shown alongside without separate texts.

question: Outer planets and lunar nodes
what_the_sources_say: GA 151 has seven moods for the seven classical planets only.
rule_the_app_follows: Uranus, Neptune, Pluto and the nodes are plotted, but are given no mood.

question: Years after 42 as a mirror of the years before 21
what_the_sources_say: Steiner gives the seven-year periods and their planets. Reading years 43–63 as a mirror of years 21 back to 1 (and years 22–42 as the turning point) comes from later biography work; George and Gisela O'Neil's life chart is drawn that way.
rule_the_app_follows: The Biography chart draws year k beside year 64 − k and says so; it draws no conclusion from the pairing.
